minutes.headline: Parks Commission backed advocating against lumping Parks into facilities for capital planning and approved a skate park letter.
minutes.summary: The commission heard director and recreation updates, discussed capital plan ranking of its three park projects, and voted to authorize the town's attorney to send a prevailing wage letter for the skate park. It also discussed town beach fees (no change decided, more data requested), Marshall Park grant paperwork, an Open Space proposal to transfer two lots to Parks, approved prior minutes, and adjourned.

public_comment.stated_role: former commission member; Finance Committee and Green Communities member
public_comment.topic: Leading a citizen initiative to preserve and renovate the cave/stone structure at Marshall Park; clarified the cave does not shorten the outfield and noted historical-structure grants.

votes.motion: Submit the letter to the Department of Labor Standards and authorize attorney Costa to act on the commission's behalf on the skate park prevailing wage matter.
Accept minutes of April 11, May 24, June 28, August 16, September 20 and October (with a correction to a vote count in September).

budget_items.what_was_said: Projects submitted for hydro raking at Marshall Pond, survey design for a field, and resurfacing of the Wallace basketball courts.
Capital committee funded permitting last year but is hesitating on further funding; commission questions partial funding.
Beach passes sold this year, with revenue and a nonresident share reported.
Beach revenue goes into the parks revolving fund, which paid for beach house repairs last year.
Member wants swim lessons self-funded; collected lesson fees were tallied against instructor pay.
Current fees recited; unchanged for about three years; compared with other towns' rates.
State grant for Marshall Park executed; commission signed project agreement.
Town spends a yearly line item to maintain the dam.
Land not permanently designated park cannot receive state park grants.

decisions.decision: Beach fee discussion continued to next meeting; staff to supply breakdown data and contact peer towns about 2024 plans.
Chair to email the capital planning committee advocating that Parks not be lumped with facilities, sharing the email with members.
Members to attend the January 16 Select Board meeting to support the Open Space recommendation.
Next meeting set for January 17 with agenda due January 11.
Commission to keep street cleanups outside its scope; organized Earth Day month cleanups on its own properties with Conservation.

what_happened.line: The commission voted to submit a prevailing wage letter on the skate park and authorize the town's attorney to act for it.
The commission discussed asking the capital planning committee not to group Parks with facilities; the chair is to email the committee.
A discussion of town beach fees ended with no change; the item was continued, with staff to bring breakdown data and check peer towns.
The state grant for Marshall Park was executed and the commission signed the project agreement.
Members plan to attend the January 16 Select Board meeting to support an Open Space recommendation to move two lots to Parks.

why_it_matters: Whether Parks is ranked as its own department or as part of facilities in capital planning can affect how its three park projects compete for capital funding.
Beach fees and swim lessons feed the parks revolving fund, so any change at the next meeting would touch what residents and nonresidents pay for beach passes.
watch_next: January 16 Select Board meeting, where members plan to support the Open Space recommendation on two lots.
January 17 Parks Commission meeting (agenda due January 11), when the beach fee discussion resumes.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the one vote (the skate park letter), the beach pass counts and revenue, and the swim lesson and beach fee figures. Our minutes record more decisions and figures than the official ones, and the attendee lists differ.
